25.explanation: Russia recognised the 'Donetsk' and 'Luhansk People's Republics' on 21 Feb 2022 and launched the full-scale invasion on 24 Feb 2022. Ukraine has never joined NATO.

26.explanation: The Kerch Strait links the enclosed Sea of Azov with the Black Sea. The Crimean Bridge built across it is the 'infrastructure' the passage mentions.

27.explanation: The ICC (Rome Statute) tries individuals for genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity and aggression. The ICJ decides disputes between States.

28.explanation: Belarus borders both Russia and Ukraine. Romania, Slovakia and Moldova border Ukraine but not Russia.

29.explanation: NATO was created by the Washington (North Atlantic) Treaty of 1949, and Article 5 is the collective-defence clause. Ukraine is a partner, not a member.

30.explanation: The war's global significance comes from its effects on energy markets, supply chains and the credibility of international institutions. The other options are factually false.

31.explanation: Judicial review (Arts. 13, 32, 226) lets courts strike down laws and executive actions that violate the Constitution.

32.explanation: The passage says electoral legitimacy remains subject to constitutional limits. Majority rule is not unlimited.

33.explanation: Separation of powers spreads power across the legislature, executive and judiciary so no organ holds unlimited power.

34.explanation: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) laid down the basic structure doctrine, which limits Parliament's amending power.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala

35.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 describe constitutionalism correctly. Statement 3 is wrong because the basic structure cannot be amended.

sources.title: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)

36.explanation: The Archaeological Survey of India conserves monuments of national importance under the AMASR Act, 1958.

37.explanation: Article 26 gives every religious denomination the right to manage its own affairs in matters of religion, subject to public order, morality and health.

38.explanation: The AMASR Act protects monuments of national importance and regulates construction in prohibited and regulated areas. It does not empower civil courts to decide ownership of all religious sites.

sources.title: Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958

39.explanation: Bhojshala at Dhar is linked to Raja Bhoja of the Paramara dynasty of Malwa (11th century).

40.explanation: Hindus regard Bhojshala as a temple of Goddess Saraswati (Vagdevi).

41.explanation: The Places of Worship (Special Provisions) Act, 1991 freezes the religious character of places of worship as it was on 15 August 1947.

sources.title: Places of Worship (Special Provisions) Act, 1991, Section 4

42.explanation: UPI is a real-time system for instant bank-to-bank fund transfers.

43.explanation: UPI was developed and is operated by the National Payments Corporation of India (launched 2016).

44.explanation: NPCI is an umbrella body for retail payments, set up by RBI and the Indian Banks' Association under the PSS Act, 2007, and operates under RBI's regulatory oversight.

sources.title: Wikipedia: National Payments Corporation of India

45.explanation: The Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 is the main law regulating payment systems in India.

46.explanation: RBI itself owns and operates NEFT (and RTGS). UPI, IMPS and RuPay are run by NPCI.

47.explanation: Feedstocks such as sugarcane and rice need a lot of water, so heavy freshwater use is the main environmental worry about scaling up ethanol.

sources.title: Passage on ethanol blending; NITI Aayog Roadmap for Ethanol Blending 2020-25

48.explanation: Ethanol made from sugarcane, grains and surplus produce gives farmers an extra market, so agriculture benefits directly.

49.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) inserted Article 48A (DPSP) and Article 51A(g) (fundamental duty) on protecting the environment.

50.explanation: The National Policy on Biofuels (2018, amended 2022) is the main policy framework for biofuels, including the 20% ethanol target.

51.explanation: SDG 7 is affordable and clean energy, the goal ethanol blending serves most directly.

52.explanation: Crops reabsorb the CO2 released when ethanol burns, which cuts net lifecycle emissions. It does not eliminate NOx or particulates.
